outages.place: Paraná, including Foz do Iguaçu, Londrina, Cascavel, Maringá, and other cities
outages.cause: Storms and two F1 tornadoes that damaged the electrical system with strong wind gusts, lightning, and fallen trees, according to Copel, with Simepar confirming the tornadoes
outages.affected: Copel, as reported by CGN in an article published at 6:47 p.m. Brasília time Saturday, Nov 21 (3:47 p.m. CT), and by Folha de Curitiba in an article published at 12:05 a.m. Brasília time Sunday, Nov 22 (9:05 p.m. CT Saturday), said that 54,246 consumer units remained without power in Paraná as of 6:30 p.m. Brasília time Saturday (3:30 p.m. CT), and that 299,603 units, or 85 percent of the customers affected by Friday's storms, had already been reconnected, with about 1,000 professionals in the field. Those reports, citing Copel, said the remaining outages at that bulletin were concentrated in the West (15,600 units), North (14,600), Northwest (10,800), Southwest (6,700), Centro-Sul and Campos Gerais (3,300), and Curitiba, the metropolitan region, and the coast (2,900). Among the cities with the most customers still out were Foz do Iguaçu (4,200), Londrina (2,800), Cascavel (2,700), Guaraqueçaba (2,000), Lapa (1,800), Apucarana (1,600), and Maringá (1,200). Copel also said a new storm on Saturday afternoon affected the East and part of the South, with the most customers then out in Guaraqueçaba (2,000), Lapa (1,800), Matinhos (445), and Paranaguá (390). Simepar confirmed two F1 tornadoes on Friday, Nov 20, one around 3:00 p.m. Brasília time (noon CT Friday) in the Vila Yolanda neighborhood of Foz do Iguaçu and another around 6:00 p.m. Brasília time (3:00 p.m. CT Friday) in Manoel Ribas, with estimated winds of 117 to 180 km/h. An earlier Copel bulletin issued at noon Saturday, as reported by Tribuna do Interior at 2:40 p.m. Brasília time Saturday (11:40 a.m. CT), said 80,588 units remained without power at that earlier hour, 273,261 had been restored (77.2 percent), and the peak had been 353,849 units at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday (5:02 p.m. CT Friday). G1, in a Jornal Nacional report published at 10:10 p.m. Brasília time Saturday (7:10 p.m. CT), said more than 50,000 houses in Paraná were still without power after the two tornadoes, and likewise reported that more than 350,000 properties had lost power on Friday night. No later official Copel remaining-outage count after the 6:30 p.m. Saturday figure of 54,246 consumer units was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday (2:55 a.m. Brasília time Sunday, Nov 22). No official firm restoration time for all remaining customers was given; Copel said work would continue until supply was restored to all affected customers.
outages.start: Afternoon and evening of Friday, Nov 20, 2026 (Brasília time), when storms and two F1 tornadoes hit Paraná; the peak of 353,849 consumer units was recorded at 8:02 p.m. Brasília time Friday (5:02 p.m. CT Friday), according to Copel's Saturday noon bulletin as reported by Tribuna do Interior

outages.place: Southern Odisha, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Kandhamal, and Boudh
outages.affected: TPSODL, as reported by OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray on Nov 20, 2026, said it had restored electricity supply to 1,069,026 consumers (written as 10,69,026 in those reports) after Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur on Friday morning, achieving 98.68 percent restoration — nearly 99 percent — across its eight-district operational area within seven hours. Those reports said all six affected 33 kV feeders, all 19 affected 33/11 kV power substations, and all 42 affected power transformers were restored, and that 364 of 365 affected 11 kV feeders and 35,749 affected distribution transformers had been restored. District-wise restoration was reported as 99.76 percent in Ganjam, 99.53 percent in Koraput, 98.90 percent in Gajapati, 98.06 percent in Rayagada, 98.01 percent in Nabarangpur, 97.55 percent in Boudh, 94.23 percent in Kandhamal, and 100 percent in Malkangiri. TPSODL CEO Amit Kumar Garg, quoted in those reports, said the company had achieved nearly 99 percent restoration. An earlier Nov 20 Odisha Stand report from Berhampur said TPSODL had reported that Cyclone Akvan affected 1,083,348 consumers across its operational area, including 534,361 in Ganjam district and 123,252 in Nabarangpur district. Later articles, including an Odisha Diary report dated Nov 21 from Berhampur and earlier Nov 20 Odisha News Online coverage, described Garg visiting cyclone-affected areas of Ganjam to review restoration and restated the same 1,083,348 affected-consumer total, including the Ganjam and Nabarangpur district figures, but did not give a later remaining-outage count or a later restoration percentage after the 98.68 percent figure. No official remaining-outage count, and no official estimated time for full restoration of remaining customers, was stated in those later reports. A New Indian Express report updated at 3:39 a.m. IST Saturday, Nov 21 (4:09 p.m. CT Friday) said power supply was disrupted in parts of the state due to the storm, with restoration work underway on a war footing in several areas of northern Odisha, including Bhadrak, Balasore and Mayurbhanj. That report did not give an official remaining-outage count for those northern districts or a later TPSODL remaining-outage count. No later official remaining-outage count or official notice of full restoration from TPSODL, TPNODL, or the Odisha government was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday (11:25 a.m. IST Sunday, Nov 22).
outages.start: Morning of Nov 20, 2026 (IST), when Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur
outages.updated: Nov 20–21, 2026, TPSODL figures via OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray (Nov 20); earlier TPSODL affected total via Odisha Stand (Nov 20); CEO restoration review via Odisha Diary (Nov 21) and Odisha News Online (Nov 20), which restated the same affected total and did not give a later remaining-outage count; New Indian Express report updated 3:39 a.m. IST Saturday, Nov 21 (= 4:09 p.m. CT Friday), on restoration work in northern Odisha including Bhadrak, Balasore and Mayurbhanj, with no official customer count; rechecked 11:55 PM CT Saturday (11:25 a.m. IST Sunday, Nov 22), no later official remaining-outage count or official notice of full restoration from TPSODL, TPNODL, or the Odisha government found

outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20 and further strikes reported on Nov 21
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, as reported by LB.ua at 10:42 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (2:42 p.m. CT), by 24tv in an article updated at 10:14 p.m. EET Saturday (2:14 p.m. CT), by OBOZ.UA at 9:59 p.m. EET Saturday (1:59 p.m. CT), by Focus at 10:59 p.m. EET Saturday (2:59 p.m. CT), by UNN at 8:20 p.m. EET Saturday (12:20 p.m. CT), and by RBC-Ukraine at 11:05 p.m. EET Saturday (3:05 p.m. CT), said that on Sunday, Nov 22, planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock in parts of the country: hourly outage schedules of 1 to 2.5 groups, or queues, for all categories of consumers, and capacity-restriction schedules for industry. Those reports, citing Ukrenergo, said the restrictions were the result of Russian attacks on the power system, that the electricity-supply situation remained difficult in Odesa and Rivne regions, where emergency restoration work was continuing, and that consumers should check current schedules on the official pages of their distribution-system operators. No official nationwide customer count was given in those Sunday-schedule announcements. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Facebook statement reported by Ukrinform at 6:22 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (10:22 a.m. CT), and by Ukrinform in English at 6:54 p.m. EET Saturday (10:54 a.m. CT), said that after the massive overnight attack on Nov 20, energy workers had managed to partially stabilize electricity supplies in the affected regions, but that enemy attacks were continuing, including deliberate strikes on energy facilities that had already been restored, and that constant air-raid alerts were significantly complicating and slowing repair work. As a result, the ministry said, the electricity supply situation in the regions may change rapidly. The ministry said that as of the evening of Nov 21, the most difficult situation remained in Odesa region, where repeated attacks on high-voltage transmission networks had caused large-scale power outages and triggered automatic protection systems. It warned that temporary voltage fluctuations or drops may occur when supply is restored. Natalia Zabolotna, head of the Vinnytsia regional military administration, as reported by Ukrinform at 10:52 a.m. EET Saturday (2:52 a.m. CT) and by NV at 10:26 a.m. EET Saturday (2:26 a.m. CT), said a Russian attack on Saturday morning had damaged an energy-infrastructure facility in Vinnytsia and that part of the city was without electricity, with energy crews working to restore supply. No official customer count was given for Vinnytsia. No official nationwide customer count, and no later official change to those Sunday all-day schedules, was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday (7:55 a.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22), when those Sunday schedules were in effect.
outages.updated: Nov 21–22, 2026, Ukrenergo Sunday Nov 22 all-day schedules of 1 to 2.5 queues, with the situation remaining difficult in Odesa and Rivne regions, via LB.ua 10:42 p.m. EET Saturday (= 2:42 p.m. CT), 24tv updated 10:14 p.m. EET Saturday (= 2:14 p.m. CT), OBOZ.UA 9:59 p.m. EET Saturday (= 1:59 p.m. CT), Focus 10:59 p.m. EET Saturday (= 2:59 p.m. CT), UNN 8:20 p.m. EET Saturday (= 12:20 p.m. CT), and RBC-Ukraine 11:05 p.m. EET Saturday (= 3:05 p.m. CT); Energy Ministry via Ukrinform 6:22 p.m. EET Saturday (= 10:22 a.m. CT) and Ukrinform English 6:54 p.m. EET Saturday (= 10:54 a.m. CT) on partial stabilization after the Nov 20 attack, continuing strikes, and the most difficult situation remaining in Odesa region as of Saturday evening; Vinnytsia OVA head Natalia Zabolotna via Ukrinform 10:52 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:52 a.m. CT) and NV 10:26 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:26 a.m. CT) on a Saturday morning strike that left part of Vinnytsia without power; rechecked 11:55 PM CT Saturday (7:55 a.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22), no official nationwide customer count and no later official change to those Sunday schedules found

outages.place: Odesa and parts of Odesa district
outages.cause: Repeated Russian attacks on high-voltage transmission networks, including a strike on a DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi energy facility on the morning of Nov 20. Ukraine's Energy Ministry said that as of the evening of Nov 21, those attacks were causing large-scale power outages in the region and triggering automatic protection systems. Ukrenergo, in Saturday evening reports on Sunday schedules, said the electricity-supply situation in Odesa region remained difficult and that emergency restoration work was continuing
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, as reported by LB.ua at 10:42 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (2:42 p.m. CT), by 24tv in an article updated at 10:14 p.m. EET Saturday (2:14 p.m. CT), and by Focus at 10:59 p.m. EET Saturday (2:59 p.m. CT), said that the electricity-supply situation remained difficult in Odesa region, where emergency restoration work was continuing, as planned Sunday, Nov 22, hourly outage schedules of 1 to 2.5 groups were announced for parts of the country. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in an official article dated Nov 21 and posted on its website, said that according to the Energy Ministry, as of the evening of Nov 21 the situation in Odesa region remained difficult. It said strikes on high-voltage, or main, transmission networks were triggering automatic protection systems, and that large-scale outages were occurring in part of Odesa district, including Odesa. It also warned that when power returns, voltage may temporarily rise or fall. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Facebook statement reported by Ukrinform at 6:22 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (10:22 a.m. CT), by LB.ua at 6:09 p.m. EET Saturday (10:09 a.m. CT), and by Suspilne at 5:14 p.m. EET Saturday (9:14 a.m. CT), likewise said that as of the evening of Nov 21 the situation in Odesa region remained difficult, that repeated Russian attacks on high-voltage transmission networks had caused large-scale power outages across the region and triggered automatic protection systems, and that temporary voltage fluctuations or drops may occur when supply is restored. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa regional military administration, as reported by Ukrinform and by RBC-Ukraine at 7:30 p.m. EET Saturday (11:30 a.m. CT), said electricity supplies in the region remained unstable after the massive attack on the energy system, and that power outages had been occurring throughout Saturday in parts of Odesa district, including the city of Odesa, because of attacks on high-voltage transmission networks. Kiper said that when electricity is unavailable, boiler houses and pumping stations may be temporarily suspended, that they are switched to backup power where technically possible, and that disruptions to heating and water supplies remain possible. Culturemeter, in a Nov 22 article, described a second day of problems with electricity and water in Odesa after the Nov 20 attack, including intermittent restoration followed by further outages, and said electric transport was not running; that report did not give an official customer count. No official Saturday evening or later customer count was given in the ministry, regional-administration, DTEK, or Sunday-schedule statements. Earlier Friday, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in an official Nov 20 evening statement, said 8,000 families in 21 settlements remained without power after the morning attack, and that crews would work overnight to restore power to another 15,600 families in 55 villages and towns after weather-damage cleanup; earlier Friday morning, 41,000 households were without power in the Odesa and Rozdilna districts, according to DTEK's press service as reported by Ukrainska Pravda and Ekonomichna Pravda. KyivPost, at 11:45 a.m. EET Saturday (3:45 a.m. CT), citing DTEK, had said emergency outages introduced on Saturday morning in Odesa and part of Odesa district were later cancelled, with a return to stabilization schedules. The later Saturday evening Energy Ministry, DTEK, and Kiper statements, together with Ukrenergo's Saturday evening note that the situation in the region remained difficult on Sunday, are the latest official status found. No official Saturday evening or later remaining-customer count was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday (7:55 a.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22).

outages.cause: Russian attack that seriously damaged energy equipment in Sarny district. Rivneoblenergo said hourly outage schedules did not apply because this was an emergency outage from the damage
outages.affected: Rivne Vechirnie (Rivnepost), in a report published at 11:00 p.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (3:00 p.m. CT), said that on Sunday, Nov 22, hourly outage schedules would be introduced in Rivne region on Ukrenergo's orders because of the difficult situation in the power system, and it listed Sunday evening queue times. The same report said that because of enemy shelling, emergency outages were currently ongoing in certain communities of the region, that energy workers were working to restore supply, and that in those settlements the hourly schedules do not apply. That Saturday night report did not give a new official remaining-settlement or customer count for Sarny district. Rivne Media, in a report published at 9:05 p.m. EET Saturday (1:05 p.m. CT), citing Rivneoblenergo, said a repeated large-scale enemy attack had significantly complicated the restoration of electricity supply in the north of Rivne region, particularly in the Sarny area. It said that as a result of yesterday's and today's drone strikes, a large number of energy facilities in the district had been damaged, and that restoration work there would continue tomorrow (Sunday, Nov 22). It said the scale of the damage, the complexity of the repairs, and security restrictions were affecting the duration of restoration. That Saturday evening report also did not give a new official remaining-settlement or customer count. Ukrenergo, as reported by LB.ua at 10:42 p.m. EET Saturday (2:42 p.m. CT) and by 24tv in an article updated at 10:14 p.m. EET Saturday (2:14 p.m. CT), also said the electricity-supply situation remained difficult in Rivne region, where emergency restoration work was continuing. The latest official remaining-settlement count found remains the Saturday morning Rivneoblenergo figure. Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne regional military administration, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 1:04 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21 (5:04 p.m. CT Friday), said that as a result of a Russian attack on Sarny district in Rivne region, 50 settlements had been left without electricity, and that constant air-raid alerts were preventing energy workers from promptly repairing the damage. Interfax-Ukraine quoted Koval's Telegram post as saying, "Half a hundred settlements have been de-energized as a result of an enemy attack on Sarny district. Constant alerts do not allow energy workers to promptly eliminate the consequences of the strike." Rivne Vechirnie (Rivnepost), in a report published at 11:35 a.m. EET Saturday (3:35 a.m. CT), citing Rivneoblenergo, said that as a result of the Russian attack and serious damage to energy equipment, 46 settlements in Sarny district remained without electricity. It said the company's specialists had been working since the previous evening to restore supply, and that constant air-raid alerts were not allowing energy workers to promptly eliminate the consequences of the strike. Rivnenski Novyny, at 10:22 a.m. EET Saturday (2:22 a.m. CT), likewise citing the situation in Sarny district, said 46 settlements had been left without electricity, that Rivneoblenergo crews had been working since the previous evening, and that hourly outage schedules did not apply because this was an emergency de-energization from damaged energy equipment. No official customer count was given. No official firm restoration time was given. No later official remaining-settlement or customer count after the Saturday morning Rivneoblenergo figure of 46 settlements was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday (7:55 a.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22).
outages.start: Evening of Nov 20, 2026 (Kyiv time), according to Rivneoblenergo as reported by Rivnepost and Rivnenski Novyny
outages.updated: Nov 21–22, 2026, Rivnepost 11:00 p.m. EET Saturday (= 3:00 p.m. CT) on Sunday hourly schedules in Rivne region and on emergency outages still ongoing in certain communities where those schedules do not apply, with no new official Sarny remaining-settlement count in that report; Rivneoblenergo via Rivne Media 9:05 p.m. EET Saturday (= 1:05 p.m. CT) on yesterday's and today's drone strikes damaging a large number of energy facilities in the Sarny area, with restoration work to continue Sunday, and with no new official remaining-settlement count in that report; Ukrenergo via LB.ua 10:42 p.m. EET Saturday (= 2:42 p.m. CT) and 24tv updated 10:14 p.m. EET Saturday (= 2:14 p.m. CT) on the situation remaining difficult in Rivne region, with emergency restoration work continuing; earlier Rivneoblenergo via Rivne Vechirnie (Rivnepost) 11:35 a.m. EET Saturday (= 3:35 a.m. CT) and Rivnenski Novyny 10:22 a.m. EET Saturday (= 2:22 a.m. CT) on 46 settlements in Sarny district still without power and on emergency rather than scheduled outages; Oleksandr Koval, Rivne regional military administration, via Interfax-Ukraine 1:04 a.m. EET Saturday (= 5:04 p.m. CT Friday) on 50 settlements; rechecked 11:55 PM CT Saturday (7:55 a.m. EET Sunday, Nov 22), no later official remaining-settlement or customer count and no official firm restoration time found

outages.place: Kurdistan Region, including Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal
outages.cause: Suspected drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field on the night of Nov 8, 2026, which halted gas production that supplies much of the region's electricity generation. Dana Gas, the field's operator, later said the facility had sustained significant damage and could produce no gas
outages.affected: Al Jazeera, on Nov 9, 2026, citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials, said a Sunday-night drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field caused a fire and left more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region without power. Omid Ahmed (also spelled Omed Ahmed), spokesperson for the Kurdistan Regional Government's Ministry of Electricity, said the attack suspended gas supply to power plants in Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Bazian, Chamchamal, and Duhok, and knocked between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of generation off the grid, Al Jazeera reported, citing the official Iraqi News Agency (INA). Rudaw later quoted Ahmed as saying that authorities had increased generation from approximately 1,000 megawatts immediately after the attack to 1,550 megawatts, of which 50 megawatts were reserved for essential facilities and factories, leaving 1,500 megawatts for residents and raising daily public electricity supply to six to eight hours, reaching nine hours in some areas. Ahmed said the electricity then available covered only 40 percent of the region's demand, leaving a 60 percent shortfall, and that no date had been established for production to resume. Rudaw's article image assets for that report are dated Nov 13, 2026. Dana Gas, in a Saturday statement reported by Rudaw, said the facility had sustained significant damage and that currently no amount of gas could be produced. 964media, in a Nov 15 report, quoted Ahmed as saying that no timeframe had been set for electricity supplies to return to normal and that the ministry was waiting for gas from Khor Mor to flow again; in that interview he also said that within 48 hours of the attack the ministry had increased generation from 1,000 megawatts to nearly 1,650 megawatts, and that some areas were then getting more than eight hours of grid power a day, particularly on holidays. The same report said grid supply had fallen to three to four hours a day right after the attack and was later raised to six to seven hours, and that Dana Gas had said the field could produce no gas. No official customer count was given. No later official generation figure, public-supply-hours update, or official confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday, Nov 21 (8:55 a.m. Iraq time Sunday, Nov 22).
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. As of the latest official statements found, no date had been established for Khor Mor production to resume.
outages.updated: Nov 8–16, 2026 attack and aftermath: Al Jazeera Nov 9 citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials and INA; KRG electricity ministry figures via Rudaw (article image assets dated Nov 13); Dana Gas still-shut statement via Rudaw and 964media; Omed Ahmed via 964media Nov 15 on no timeframe for a return to normal supply and on generation rising to nearly 1,650 megawatts within 48 hours of the attack; rechecked 11:55 PM CT Saturday, Nov 21 (8:55 a.m. Iraq time Sunday, Nov 22), no later official generation figure or confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed found

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Debaltseve, Snizhne, and nearby districts
outages.cause: Local accidents and a power deficit, according to the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, including a Friday evening equipment failure in Donetsk that the ministry later said had been restored early Sunday, a Saturday evening disruption that the ministry attributed to combat in a neighboring region, and Sunday morning automatic disconnections and network overloads in Donetsk city reported by occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin
outages.affected: Occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin, as reported by Vesti at 8:22 a.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (11:22 p.m. CT Saturday if the time is Moscow time), said all districts of Donetsk were partially without power and that more than 40,000 subscribers were without electricity. Vesti quoted Kulemzin's message in the MAX messenger as saying that 347 transformer substations had disconnected automatically, leaving 36,655 subscribers without electricity, and that, because permissible network load had been exceeded, 58 transformer substations had also been disconnected in all districts of Donetsk, leaving 4,700 subscribers without electricity. The report said emergency crews were working at the sites and did not give a restoration time. That Sunday morning city figure came after an earlier occupation-ministry statement, reported by Vzglyad at 1:05 a.m. Sunday, Nov 22 (4:05 p.m. CT Saturday if Moscow time) and by Life.ru, quoting TASS, that energy workers had completed restoration work in the Donetsk city district and that all consumers previously disconnected as a result of the accident had been reconnected to electricity. Vzglyad noted that on Saturday more than 67,000 subscribers in Donetsk had been left without electricity because of emergency outages and network overload. The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, in a Saturday evening statement reported by RIA Novosti at 8:35 p.m. Saturday, Nov 21 (11:35 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time), had said that as a result of combat actions by Ukrainian forces in a neighboring region, electricity supply had been disrupted in a way that affected part of the occupied Donetsk region's territory. The ministry said the list of urban and municipal districts without electricity, and the scale of the damage in the neighboring region, were still being clarified, and that in Donetsk city energy workers were continuing work to reconnect consumers left without power after an accident. That Saturday evening statement did not give a new official region-wide remaining-customer count. The latest official region-wide remaining total found remains the occupation ministry's Saturday morning figure. The ministry, in a Saturday morning statement reported by DNR News at 10:12 a.m. Saturday (1:12 a.m. CT if Moscow time), and citing Donetskenergo, said that as of 7:00 a.m. Saturday, Nov 21 (10:00 p.m. CT Friday if that time is Moscow time), more than 107,000 subscribers in the occupied region remained without power. The same Saturday morning statement said that around 7:00 p.m. Friday, Nov 20 (10:00 a.m. CT Friday if Moscow time), a failure in electrical-network equipment had left part of Donetsk without electricity, and that partial outages also continued in Makiivka, Mariupol, Yenakiieve, Horlivka, Debaltseve, and the Yasynuvata, Amvrosiivka, Volnovakha, Telmanove, and Volodarske municipal districts because of a shortage of available capacity and local emergency situations. No later official region-wide remaining total after the 7:00 a.m. Saturday figure of more than 107,000 subscribers was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday (8:55 a.m. Moscow time Sunday, Nov 22).
outages.start: Around 7:00 p.m. Friday, Nov 20, 2026 (10:00 a.m. CT Friday if Moscow time), for the Donetsk city equipment failure described by the occupation ministry; other partial outages in the region were already being reported
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The Sunday morning Kulemzin statement reported by Vesti said emergency crews were working and did not say when supply would be restored.

outages.place: Crimea, including Dzhankoy, Yevpatoria, and Bilohirsk
outages.cause: A power-capacity shortage after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula, according to occupation sources, and consumption restrictions introduced on Saturday, Nov 21, on orders of the Russian federal System Operator, according to Krymenergo
outages.affected: Krymenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 11:40 a.m. Saturday, Nov 21 (2:40 a.m. CT if Moscow time), said that on Saturday six districts and three cities on the peninsula were without power, for an estimated three hours, because of introduced restrictions on electricity supply. It said residents were without power in villages of the Rozdolne, Sovietskyi, Saky, Pervomaiske, Kirovske, and Dzhankoy districts, that 75 streets and lanes in Dzhankoy were without power, that 36 streets in Yevpatoria were without power, and that 44 streets and three garden partnerships in Bilohirsk were without power. The same report said consumption-mode restrictions had been introduced on Saturday and that lights would be turned off in populated places for three to six hours. An earlier Krymenergo statement, reported by RIA Novosti Crimea at 9:06 a.m. Saturday (12:06 a.m. CT if Moscow time) and by News-CR at 8:51 a.m. Saturday (11:51 p.m. CT Friday if Moscow time), said the Saturday restrictions were introduced on orders of the Russian federal System Operator, that the approximate duration of the outages was 3 to 6 hours, that if the outage periods were extended or additional restrictions were introduced further information would be published, and that at that earlier hour power was already out in parts of Bilohirsk and the Rozdolne and Sovietskyi districts, with a planned restoration there in about three hours. No official customer count was given. Occupation sources have said peninsula-wide interruptions began Oct 24, 2026, after strikes on transmission networks outside the peninsula, and that additional restrictions followed a later attack on Nov 4. The same Saturday RIA Novosti Crimea coverage said that because of an insufficient volume of incoming electricity, schedules for the supply of electricity and water had been introduced in Crimea and Sevastopol, and that electricity was being supplied depending on technical capability. Those Saturday 3-to-6-hour restrictions were described as applying on Saturday; no official Sunday, Nov 22, peninsula-wide restriction list, and no official notice that the general deficit-related supply restrictions had been lifted, was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday (8:55 a.m. Moscow time Sunday, Nov 22).
outages.start: Occupation sources said peninsula-wide interruptions began Oct 24, 2026; Saturday's additional 3-to-6-hour restrictions were reported Nov 21, 2026
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, Krymenergo via RIA Novosti Crimea 11:40 a.m. Saturday (= 2:40 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on six districts and three cities, including 75 streets and lanes in Dzhankoy, 36 streets in Yevpatoria, and 44 streets in Bilohirsk, and on Saturday 3-to-6-hour consumption restrictions; earlier Krymenergo via RIA Novosti Crimea 9:06 a.m. Saturday (= 12:06 a.m. CT if Moscow time) and News-CR 8:51 a.m. Saturday (= 11:51 p.m. CT Friday if Moscow time) on System Operator orders, on a planned restoration in about three hours for places already out that morning, and on an ongoing incoming-power shortage and supply schedules since Oct 24; rechecked 11:55 PM CT Saturday (8:55 a.m. Moscow time Sunday, Nov 22), no official Sunday peninsula-wide restriction list, no official notice that general deficit-related restrictions had been lifted, and no official customer count, found

outages.cause: Generation-capacity deficit in the national electric system. UNE's Saturday bulletin said unit 8 of CTE Mariel, units 1 and 2 of CTE Santa Cruz, and unit 2 of CTE Felton were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance, with thermal-generation limitations of 394 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Saturday bulletin, published by Cubadebate on Saturday, Nov 21, and also reported by Juventud Rebelde, which posted the same official figures at 8:36 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (7:36 a.m. CT) and updated the article at 8:54 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (7:54 a.m. CT), said the national electric system continued to face a generation-capacity deficit. It said service had been affected by a capacity deficit throughout all 24 hours on Friday, Nov 20, and that the affectation continued through the early morning, with a maximum affectation of 1,799 MW recorded at 7:10 p.m. Cuba time Friday (6:10 p.m. CT Friday). It said solar-photovoltaic parks produced 4,177 MWh, with a maximum of 650 MW delivered in the midday period. At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Saturday, Nov 21 (5:00 a.m. CT), the bulletin said SEN availability was 980 MW against demand of 2,270 MW, with 1,295 MW affected. For the midday period it estimated an affectation of 1,400 MW. For the evening peak, UNE estimated that unit 8 of CTE Mariel would enter with 45 MW, and it forecast availability of 1,025 MW against a maximum demand of 2,800 MW, a deficit of 1,775 MW, and, if those conditions held, an affectation of 1,805 MW at the peak. Official UNE sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid. No official Saturday evening-peak actual from UNE was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday (12:55 a.m. Cuba time Sunday, Nov 22), after the typical Saturday evening-peak period had ended. No official UNE Sunday bulletin was found; Sunday morning had only just begun in Cuba at the time of this update.
outages.updated: Nov 21, 2026, UNE Saturday bulletin via Cubadebate and Juventud Rebelde, posted 8:36 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (= 7:36 a.m. CT) and updated 8:54 a.m. Cuba time Saturday (= 7:54 a.m. CT), including the official Friday evening-peak actual of 1,799 MW at 7:10 p.m. Cuba time Friday (= 6:10 p.m. CT Friday), Saturday 6:00 a.m. Cuba time figures of 980 MW available, 2,270 MW demand, and 1,295 MW affected, and a Saturday evening-peak forecast affectation of 1,805 MW; rechecked 11:55 PM CT Saturday (12:55 a.m. Cuba time Sunday, Nov 22), no official Saturday evening-peak actual from UNE and no official Sunday UNE bulletin found

outages.cause: Fuel shortages affecting electricity generation, according to the state electricity company Tavanir
outages.affected: Nour News, in a report dated 8:09 a.m. Iran time Sunday, Nov 22, or 1 Azar 1405 (10:39 p.m. CT Saturday), and Eghtesad Online, in a report dated 8:29 a.m. Iran time Sunday (10:59 p.m. CT Saturday) that cited Nour News, said planned electricity restrictions began today, the first of Azar, and attributed that announcement to the chief executive of Tavanir, the state electricity company. Those reports said the restrictions were being imposed because of special fuel-supply conditions and the need to manage consumption, in order to help keep the power network stable. They said, citing the Tavanir chief executive, that the new restrictions may take the form of a two-hour outage over two days, or a maximum of two hours each day, and that the timing is not fixed and may change with network conditions. They said customers would be informed of outage times through the Bargh-e Man system and app, the Bale messenger app, and text messages. Tavanir had announced on Saturday, Nov 21, that planned electricity restrictions on households and businesses would begin on Sunday, Nov 22, because fuel shortages were disrupting power generation, according to Iran International in a report dated 5:11 p.m. GMT Saturday, Nov 21 (11:11 a.m. CT), and to RFE/RL in a report dated midnight CET Sunday, Nov 22 (5:00 p.m. CT Saturday). Iran International, citing Tavanir, quoted Tavanir chief executive Mohammad Allahdad as saying that outages could last up to two hours every two days, and could increase to two hours daily as temperatures fall, and that the country's gas production remained below last year's levels. Anar News, in a report updated at 12:05 a.m. UTC Sunday, Nov 22 (6:05 p.m. CT Saturday), citing BBC Persian, also said planned power outages began in Iran on Sunday, Nov 22, because of fuel shortages at power plants. No official customer count was given in those reports. No official nationwide remaining-customer count was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday (9:25 a.m. Iran time Sunday, Nov 22).

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Drop Site News, in a Nov 20, 2026 report from Khartoum, said a particularly intense wave of drone strikes at the end of October and into November targeting power stations, fuel supplies, and electricity infrastructure had brought the country's power grid to the brink of collapse, and that two weeks after the wave of attacks, major substations remained out of service. Shaker Ismail, an engineer with the Sudanese Electricity Company, told Drop Site that repairing some of the country's most important power facilities could take months or longer, that high-capacity transformers and digital control systems had been damaged, and that replacement transformers must be manufactured to order abroad. Ismail said the Um Dabakir thermal power plant in White Nile State was badly damaged in an Oct 29 strike and forced to shut down, and that the Al-Markhiyat substation west of Omdurman was put out of service after an Oct 27 strike; he said affected areas continued to experience prolonged outages and scheduled power cuts as of this week. The report said the Sudan Electricity Holding Company and Ministry of Energy had yet to publicly announce the restoration of the major facilities damaged in the attacks. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. An earlier Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature said there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day, and, citing The Associated Press, said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found as of 11:55 PM CT Saturday.
